description.1: DevOps and IaC lead for two programmes at once: the Chalfont data-centre exit to AWS Frankfurt and the Lot 1 / Wingman landing zone in Stockholm. Authored 281 of 549 pull requests (51%) across 37 repositories; RWS engineers reviewed and merged 251 of my 252 merged PRs.

The estate runs 22 workspaces and 4,400+ resources with 0 errored.

case_study.problem: RWS had to exit a data centre and stand up a second, separate landing zone at the same time, on a flat AWS estate with no infrastructure as code, where RWS engineers merge and apply every change.
case_study.built: Led DevOps and IaC: org governance, account baselines, Identity Center and both Transit Gateway network hubs as HCP Terraform code, 281 of the 549 PRs across 37 repos.
decisions: A separate Stockholm hub with its own TGW ASN, sharing one module library
Tag-driven firewall access through hub-owned prefix lists and one writer
AWS IPAM with prefix delegation, enforced by a CreateVpc-only SCP
Every change applied in a sandbox mirror first, same least-privilege role
case_study.outcome: 22 workspaces and 4,400+ resources with 0 errored, 251 of 252 PRs merged by RWS engineers, and new workload networks onboarded in about 15 minutes.

case_study.problem: Medical image classification needed an automated path from data processing and multi-model training to production endpoints that update without downtime.

Blue-green endpoint deployment with auto-scaling and drift detection
CloudFront frontend with an API Gateway and Lambda inference API
case_study.outcome: The endpoints support zero-downtime model updates with automatic rollback, and the work was generalized and published by AWS as an official sample under aws-samples (MIT-0).
